evals.prompt: My React app stores the JWT access token in localStorage for API requests.
evals.expected_output: Violation: Never store secrets in localStorage — XSS-vulnerable. Any script on the page can read localStorage. Fix: store JWT in HttpOnly Secure cookies — inaccessible to JavaScript. Use SameSite=Strict for CSRF protection. Configure the server to set the cookie on login. Pass session state (user object) to React, never the raw token.

evals.prompt: A user can view other users' private data by changing the user ID in the URL. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) — a backend issue, not a frontend one. No Client Logic for Permissions: validate ownership on the backend. The API must verify request.user.id === resource.userId before returning data. Frontend validation is for UX only — never rely on it for security. Add server-side auth guard to every data endpoint.

evals.prompt: My React app has 12 npm dependencies. I haven't updated them in 6 months.
evals.expected_output: Run npm audit or pnpm audit to find known CVEs. Pin specific dependency versions. Use npm-check-updates to find available updates. Check for high/critical severity advisories and update immediately. Regular dependency audits are part of React application hardening. Also check for dependencies with security headers compliance.
